exposure: Maternal super obesity (body mass index [BMI] ≥ 50 kg/m(2))
Maternal BMI at delivery (18.5 to 29.9 kg/m(2), 30 to 39.9 kg/m(2), 40 to 49.9 kg/m(2), and ≥ 50 kg/m(2))
outcome: Acute neonatal morbidity (5-minute Apgar score < 5, cardiopulmonary resuscitation and ventilator support < 24 hours, neonatal injury, and/or transient tachypnea of the newborn)

Severe neonatal morbidity (grade 3 or 4 intraventricular hemorrhage, necrotizing enterocolitis, seizure, respiratory distress syndrome, hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy, meconium aspiration, ventilator support ≥ 2 days, sepsis and/or neonatal death)
cohort: Singleton neonates delivered via cesarean delivery ≥ 37 weeks in the Maternal-Fetal Medicine Unit Cesarean Registry
finding: Maternal super obesity is associated with increased risk of acute and severe neonatal morbidity among term infants delivered via CD.
mod_finding: The study focused specifically on neonatal outcomes for infants born via cesarean delivery, and did not compare different modes of delivery.
